result:
Post revisions are in place and `pnpm typecheck` passes. I did not boot the app or exercise the routes over HTTP, so the behaviour is untested beyond types.

Every successful edit now snapshots the post's previous title, excerpt and body into a new `post_revisions` table, in one D1 batch with the update. Create and refused edits keep nothing. `GET /posts/:id/revisions` lists revisions newest first, and `POST /posts/:id/revisions/:revisionId/restore` restores one and keeps the pre-restore version as a new revision. Both routes are author-only: guests go to `/login`, other users get 403, and a revision from another post gets 404. Deleting a post also deletes its revisions. The post page links to the revisions page for the author.

Changes are in `db/schema.ts` with a generated migration (`db/migrations/20261019224815_numerous_maximus.sql`), `lib/revisions.ts` (new), `lib/validators.ts`, `pages/posts/[id].server.ts` and `pages/posts/[id].tsx`, plus the new `pages/posts/[id]/revisions.{server.ts,tsx}` and `routes/posts/[id]/revisions/[revisionId]/restore.ts`.

Separately, the existing `DELETE /posts/:id` action never checks that the caller is the author, so any signed-in user can delete anyone's post. I left that alone because it is outside this task, but it is worth fixing.
